eligibility_criteria: LVEF <25% and unable to exercise for HF or, if able to perform cardiopulmonary exercise testing, with peak VO2 <12 mL/kg/min and/or <50% predicted value.
≥3 HF hospitalizations in previous 12 months without an obvious precipitating cause.
Dependence on i.v. inotropic therapy or temporary MCS.

Progressive end-organ dysfunction (worsening renal and/or hepatic function, type II pulmonary hypertension, cardiac cachexia) due to reduced perfusion and not to inadequately low ventricular filling pressure (PCWP >20 mmHg and SBP <90 mmHg or cardiac index <2 L/min/m2).

psychosocial_and_contraindications.psychosocial_requirement: Stable psychosocial background with demonstrated understanding of the technology and patient living with a caregiver; living alone or poor psychosocial background is LVAD contraindication.

studies_and_outcomes_summary: Current 2-year survival rates with latest continuous-flow LVADs comparable to heart transplantation; actuarial survival reported ~80% at 1 year and ~70% at 2 years in some series.

MOMENTUM 3: two-year survival 84.5%; survival free of disabling stroke or need for reoperation for LVAD malfunction 76.9% with a centrifugal-flow LVAD. Need for reoperation for malfunction ~2.3% per 24 months; pump replacement due to thrombosis ~0.6% per 24 months.
ELEVATE registry (real-world, centrifugal-flow LVAD): overall survival 74.5% at 2 years; gastrointestinal bleeding 9.7%; stroke 10.2%; pump thrombosis 1.5%.

IMACS Registry: proposed composite endpoint including QOL and adverse events; 'living well at one year' (freedom from death, stroke, bleeding requiring operation, RV assist device, pump replacement, or device-related infection within first year) was 56.8% for isolated centrifugal-flow LVAD in one report.

REMATCH (outdated): only RCT comparing LVAD as destination therapy (DT) with OMT in advanced HF NYHA class IV; showed lower all-cause mortality with LVAD vs medical treatment but high 2-year mortality in both arms.
content.devices_and_technology_notes: Fully magnetically levitated centrifugal-flow LVADs have significantly reduced pump thrombosis and some adverse events compared with older devices. Incidence of overall bleeding events, thromboembolism and driveline infection remained similar to older devices in some comparisons.
content.references_and_supplements: Details of devices and long-term MCS studies summarized in Supplementary Table 15. Multiple trials/registries cited include MOMENTUM 3, ELEVATE, IMACS, REMATCH, ADVANCE, ENDURANCE.
